newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat emergence sharply ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat emergence sharply ahead of average.

text.p: Emergence of winter wheat in Texas was sharply ahead of average during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
Dry weather allowed producers to make good progress on planting and harvesting operations.
Warm days and cool nights provided good drying and crop maturity conditions until a late-week cold front brought the first frost to the High Plains area of the state.
Harvesting of cotton increased in the Plains, and early yields were said to be high. Bolls were opening rapidly until the cool weather arrived late in the week.
Wheat planted 91 percent vs 85 week ago, 70 year ago, 73 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 78 pct vs 69 w/a, 36 y/a, 44 avg.
Corn harvested 94 pct vs 91 w/a, 91 y/a, 95 avg.
Sorghum harvested 71 pct vs 68 w/a, 88 y/a, 83 avg.
Sorghum mature 97 pct vs 94 w/a, 97 y/a, 93 avg.
Sorghum rated 66 pct good/excellent vs 65 w/a.
Cotton bolls opening 87 pct vs 75 w/a, 76 y/a, 75 avg.
Cotton harvested 24 pct vs 21 w/a, 37 y/a, 37 avg.
Cotton rated 49 pct good/excellent vs 49 w/a.
Pasture and range condition 46 pct good to excellent, versus 52 percent at that level last week.
